summary: Under one roof, or not: {the partner} asks to share a roof, to marry, or to end it, and the household has to rearrange around the answer.
realLife: One life: A restaurant owner and a woman he met at an engagement party in 1971 married about a week later. He moved in with her, her mother and her grandfather until they could afford their own home. Her mother opposed it at first and later came to love him, and they were still together near their fiftieth anniversary. Another: After three months together he proposed during a recorded interview, using the ring his late father had used. She said yes. They married, stayed together nearly twenty years and have two sons. Another: A mother who divorced through a mediator tells another who is divorcing how she and her ex told their daughter together, sitting on the floor and stressing routines that stay the same. They share custody on a written plan and stayed on civil terms. Another: Her son, twelve, recalls the yelling at home before his parents' 2009 divorce, being torn, and his grades slipping for two school years. He now spends alternate weeks with each parent and mostly wants his mother to be happy.
